reviews.title: For new SSD buyers:  Test Seagate’s SeaTools first.  When, how to buy a matching PC.
reviews.comment: As I heard that whining sound, I feared that my PC's four-years-old standard hard drive was dying.  My future direction is toward video-editing, requiring a faster PC (gaming PCs are also used for video editing).  Why not acquire this high-speed Seagate Fire to match my soon-to-purchase PC? When will my current hard drive crash?  When will I need a Firecuda matching PC?  How do I buy a matching PC?  These might be common questions other potential buyers have. My first step should have been to software test my existing standard hard drive instead of my relying on the traditional technique of listening to hard disk sounds and evaluating the hard drive's age.  Seagate provides a wonderful, free diagnostics software, SeaTools, which takes less than 15 minutes to learn!  SeaTools thoroughly checked my hard drive's data integrity.  I no longer fear an impending hard drive crash, thus alleviating the time pressure I felt while shopping for a high-performance PC. What PC specifications match this Firecuda 510?  Form Factor: M.2 2280 double-sided.  PCIe Gen 3 ×4, NVMe 1.3 .  And, if motherboard manufacturers specs are available-- a max sequential read of 3450 megabytes per second and max sequential write of 3200 megabytes per second.  Firecuda 520 is PCIe Generation 4, still faster. Seagate's pre-sales and tech support are very helpful with specifications.  PC manufacturers may be cool on helping you match specs. Good luck! Seagate's SeaTools and support staff alleviated my hard-drive-crash anxiety and quickly diagnosed my hard drive.  I now have time to carefully purchase the video-editing, gaming PC to best match my needs with Firecuda.  When the video-editing, gaming PC arrives, I'll update its performance with Firecuda.  Until then, my 4 stars is for proven excellent support.
reviews.author: Chen Sun
